abstract: Plant Resistance Genes database (PRGdb) 5.0 (https://prgdb.org/prgdb5/) is a major update of the PRGdb, designed to expand plant disease resistance gene resources within a unified web platform. The release incorporates predictions for 97 plant proteomes and adds 288, 315 new putative resistance-associated proteins, bringing the database to 874,967 candidate resistance proteins from 279 plant proteomes. The curated reference collection increased from 199 to 462 experimentally supported resistance proteins. To complement domain-based classification, the platform introduces an AI-assisted prioritization layer powered by the Deep Resistance gene Evaluator Model (DREM), a deep learning model that evaluates amino acid sequences to predict resistance-associated features. DREM provides an overall resistance score, domain-level probabilities, a Structural Confidence Score, and a composite prioritization score, assigning proteins to five prioritization categories. Furthermore, PRGdb 5.0 bridges genomic sequences with functional data by transforming gene entries into connected evidence hubs. Through dynamic API integrations, individual gene pages embed real-time external data, including STRING protein interaction networks, Reactome pathways, Expression Atlas tissue profiles, and standardized Gene Ontology annotations. A redesigned interface supports multicriteria searches with Boolean operators, bulk downloads, and a live literature news feed. Together, these updates provide a scalable platform supporting the workflow from sequence analysis to target protein identification.
